name: mx-fibra-trust
display_name: Mexico FIBRA — Contrato de Fideicomiso (Trust Agreement)
description: A print-first (WeasyPrint) Mexican FIBRA Contrato de Fideicomiso (Trust Agreement) template — a Spanish-language civil-law notarial instrument, structurally the Mexico expression of the Woodfine Direct-Hold Solution's constitutional document (the Canada LP Agreement's counterpart). Retypeset against the executed FIBRA SOMA (CIB/3332) Contrato de Fideicomiso precedent. Carries civil-law-specific structure with no analogue among the other Paper families: a portada framed by two heavy rules, an Índice with dot-leaders, flowing Secciones/Cláusulas (no forced page break per section), incisos enumerated with a parenthetical (a)/(i) counter, a Definiciones hanging-indent glossary, comité-roster tables, and Anexos.

variants.name: portada
variants.description: Cover framed by two heavy rules (hr.portada-rule, 2.25pt); centered title/subtitle; parties stacked as "como <rol>" lines (Fideicomitente, Fiduciario, Representante Común, plus comparecencia of Administrador and Asesor); place/date line with honest [●] fill-ins.

variants.name: indice
variants.description: Auto-computed table of contents (Índice), dot-leader convention, right-aligned page numbers injected by build-pdf.py's "shape 3" render (cover + Índice + body renumbered from 1); own dedicated page.

variants.name: body-secciones
variants.description: Secciones I–XVII, flowing continuously (SOMA-verified — do NOT force a page break per Sección); each Sección heading centered/bold/underlined; each Cláusula heading run-in at the 26pt notarial indent.

variants.name: enumerated-incisos
variants.description: The three-legged inciso mechanism: parenthetical counter glyph ((a), (i)), the shared 26pt indent grid, and list-style-position: inside — all three legs are load-bearing together.

variants.name: definiciones
variants.description: Sección I hanging-indent glossary (p.gloss), 26pt hanging entry.

variants.name: comite-roster
variants.description: Governance tables (Comité Técnico / Auditoría / Prácticas Societarias): Nombre | Carácter | Independiente columns, .comite-indep centered Sí/No cell.

variants.name: firmas
variants.description: Signature blocks as table.signature-block (never a bordered div — a CSS-border line does not survive to Word), one block per signatory role: El Fideicomitente, El Fiduciario, El Representante Común, El Administrador, El Asesor.

variants.name: anexo
variants.description: Anexos A–E (Portafolio Inicial, Formato del Título, Miembros del Comité Técnico, Formato del Contrato de Administración, Escrow/Esquema de Compensaciones); each a simple descriptive list, not a paginated sub-document — no per-Anexo restart numbering, deliberately not applied since these are short integral lists.

aria: Índice entries are real anchor-equivalent structural navigation (dot-leader + page number, not decorative); signature blocks are real <table> markup with cell-level text, not rasterized images, so they remain selectable/screen-reader-legible in the PDF. The <mark>[●]</mark> placeholder sentinel is a genuine fill-in-later marker, not decorative highlighting — must remain in the accessibility tree distinguishably from settled text.

wcag.note: Pure black-on-white register (no color-only meaning anywhere); the placeholder-mark's soft amber (#FDF3B3) is a visibility aid on top of real text, not a substitute for it.

motion: Print-first static document — no interaction states; renders to PDF via WeasyPrint 61.x via project-documents/bin/build-pdf.py "shape 3" (cover + Índice + body renumbered from 1, split-and-merge workaround for WeasyPrint's counter-reset: page limitation).
open_questions: oq-1: should the Índice/cover/portada conventions established here become the shared house default for all future Mexican civil-law instruments (of which this is the first), or are they trust-specific? Not decidable from one document.

oq-2: this recipe and mx-fibra-prospectus share the body type register, the soft placeholder mark, and the draft-stamp convention but differ in page geometry and section taxonomy — landed as a coordinated pair per both drafts' recommendation.
